Al rond 1400 stond hier, buiten de Molen: As early as 1400 a chapel stood here, outside the Molenpoort gate, where Saint Rumbold was called on against the evil eye, sore throats and cattle disease. Today's chapel is from the 18th century; the lime trees around it were planted in 1838. Since its restoration in 1975 it is the memorial chapel for the people of Weert who died in the Second World War, with a work by Felix van Kalmthout: Lest we forget.
Al sinds 1836 werden hier houten schepen: Wooden ships had been repaired here since 1836. In 1907 the Weerter Scheepsbouw Maatschappij started building steel ships; 145 were launched up to 1947. In the 1920s Driessens drew the Weert kempenaar: a barge 50 metres long and 6.60 wide, which at 525 tonnes carried just a little more than an ordinary kempenaar. In its best year the yard delivered thirteen and employed two hundred men.
Beltmolen uit 1904, gebouwd nadat de sta: A mound mill of 1904, built after the post mill on this spot was struck by lightning and burnt down. It ground grain until just before the Second World War. At the restoration of 1961 it got its name, after the grandfather of the millwright. It is a restaurant now; the mill can still turn.
Bij de bouw van de wijk Molenakker vonde: When the Molenakker neighbourhood was built, amateur archaeologists found Roman bronze vessels. The excavation of 1994 uncovered a fortification of one and a half hectares from the first century BC: a refuge with a ditch three metres wide, in the time of the Eburones. Beside it, until about AD 250, lay a settlement of at least ten hectares, with 45 larger buildings and six wells.
Bourgondische heren aan tafel, met Walbu: Burgundian lords at table, with Walburgis van Nieuwenaer, the wife of Philip of Horne. One of the murals painted in the old town in 2018.
De Beesterbrök verbindt de Biest met Mol: The Beesterbrök links the Biest with Molenakker. Before that neighbourhood was built, the road from the town to the village of Laar ran here. Today's drawbridge was built in 1997 where an old cast-iron bridge of the same kind stood.

De Peel-Raamstelling, in 1939 aangelegd,: The Peel-Raam line, laid out in 1939, ran from the Maas at Grave through the Peel and along the Zuid-Willemsvaart to the Belgian border near Weert. Along the canal the concrete casemates stood every two hundred metres, mostly at the bridges. Three still stand on the Noordkade. On the morning of 11 May 1940 there was a short fight near Weert; by then the line had already fallen.

De Van Hornekazerne is in 1938 gebouwd a: The Van Horne barracks were built in 1938 as one of sixteen standard barracks for the infantry. In May 1940 the soldiers left for the Peel-Raam line along the canal; the barracks stood empty and the occupier moved in. After the liberation the English came, and in November 1944 Eisenhower paid a visit. From 1951 every non-commissioned officer of the army was trained here, at the Onderofficiersschool, which has been Royal since 1961.

De heren van Horne kregen in de 12e eeuw: In the 12th century the lords of Horne gained more and more say in Weert. A charter of 1295 mentions the house of count Willem II of Horne; a year later he was allowed to draw off water to fill its moat. Whether it was a castle or only a manor, nobody knows for sure. In 2020 a burial vault was found here in which Philip of Horne may have been buried.

De kerk van de nieuwbouwwijk Moesel, die: The church of the new Moesel neighbourhood, which became a rectorate in 1963. First the Moesel chapel served as a temporary church, then a temporary church on Christinelaan. The low brick building with a flat roof and no tower, by the architect P.W.J. Coenders, was finished in 1972. Gène Eggen made the wall of stained glass.

De onthoofding van Philips van Horne in: The beheading of Philip of Horne in Brussels, on 5 June 1568. One of the murals painted in the old town in 2018, 450 years after his death.

De paters van de Heilige Geest kwamen in: The Holy Ghost Fathers came to Weert from Lier in 1904 to train missionaries; their boarding school grew from thirty to some two hundred pupils. The chapel, designed by Pierre Cuypers Jr., was finished in 1911. The school closed in 1970 and the mission house was torn down, but the chapel stayed: it is now the Turkish mosque.
De pijpenfabriek Trumm-Bergmans kwam in: The pipe factory Trumm-Bergmans came to Weert in 1855 and a year later built this kiln of brick and fireclay to fire clay pipes. In 1933 the factory switched to briar pipes; from then on the kiln burnt the wood waste. In 1989 it was moved fifty metres, to the Biest bridge.
De protestanten van Weert moesten lang n: For a long time the Protestants of Weert had to walk to Budel for church. In 1852 they got a congregation of their own, which met in a house on the Oelemarkt. This octagonal church was built from 1910 to 1912 to a design by George van Heukelom, the architect of the station. Above the door it says: Surely the Lord is in this place.

De waaiervormige kerk van baksteen en be: The fan-shaped church of brick and concrete gave the Fatima neighbourhood its name; before that the workers' district was called Molenveld. It was designed by the Weert architect Pierre Weegels and finished in 1955. Since 2011 it is no longer a parish church: as the Fatimahuis it serves the neighbourhood, and on Sundays the Eritrean Orthodox church holds its service here.
Een laatgotische hallenkerk: drie beuken: A late Gothic hall church: three aisles of equal height under one roof. The Netherlands has two left, this one and the Grote Kerk in Zwolle. The choir was finished in 1456, the nave in 1512, and in 1528 work on the tower began. The vaults are painted from front to back. In 1887 the tower got a spire reaching 104.80 metres, then the third tallest in the Netherlands. It came down in an autumn storm in 1940. Today's crown, by Theo Verlaan, is from 1960.
Een van de muurschilderingen die in 2018: One of the murals painted in the old town in 2018, 450 years after the death of Philip de Montmorency, count of Horne.
Gebouwd in 1876 in Duitse neogotiek voor: Built in 1876 in German Gothic Revival for the Ursuline sisters, driven out of Dorsten in Germany by the Kulturkampf. In Weert they started a boarding school (1883) and a school (1895). The sisters left in 1989; only the main building and the chapel of Mary were kept and became shops.
Heilig Hartbeeld van de beeldhouwer Augu: A Sacred Heart statue by the sculptor August Falise.

Het kerkhof van de Sint-Martinuskerk lig: The churchyard of Saint Martin's lies a few hundred metres from the church, outside the old Molenpoort gate, next to Saint Rumbold's chapel. It also has a wall for urns.

Hier werd in 1442 het klooster Maria Wij: The convent Maria Wijngaard was founded here in 1442, for canonesses of Saint Augustine. The French dissolved it in 1797. In 1843 Bridgettine sisters from Uden moved in, and that is what it still is: a Bridgettine convent, with a chapel of 1843 on the street and a statue of Saint Bridget above the gate.
In 1306 droeg het kapittel van Sint-Serv: In 1306 the chapter of Saint Servatius in Maastricht handed its rights in Weert to the lords of Horne. From that year until 1568 coins were struck in Weert. The graceful curved front of the Mint House is younger, from 1580 or shortly after. The quarter around it was torn down for the Muntpassage shopping centre (1970); only this house was left. In 2003 it was the model for KLM's 84th Delft Blue house.
In 1414 kreeg Weert marktrechten. Onder: In 1414 Weert was granted market rights. Under the protection of the counts of Horne the town flourished between 1450 and 1550, above all through the cloth that was woven here. The church on the Markt dates from that time.
In 1974 opgericht als Cultureel Centrum: Founded in 1974 as Cultureel Centrum De Munt, above the Muntpassage shopping centre. The hall and the balcony seat 459 together; some 50,000 people visit each year.
Jacob I van Horne liet tussen 1455 en 14: Between 1455 and 1461 Jacob I of Horne had a new moated castle built against the town wall: the Nijenborgh, the new castle. It measured 75 by 60 metres, with four corner towers and a tall residential wing with stepped gables. In the Eighty Years' War it was besieged time and again, and in 1702, in the War of the Spanish Succession, destroyed. On the foundations of the south tower the house Op de Biest has stood since 1841.
Kapel uit 1912 aan het Moeselplein, gewi: A chapel of 1912 on Moeselplein, dedicated to Our Lady of Lourdes. When the Moesel neighbourhood was built in the 1960s, it briefly served as its temporary church.

Meelfabriek pal aan de Zuid-Willemsvaart: A flour mill right on the Zuid-Willemsvaart, with a harbour crane on the quay to unload the barges. The complex is a national monument.

Monument voor de vastelaovendj van Jan v: A monument to carnival, vastelaovendj, by Jan van Riet. At carnival the people of Weert are called Rogstaekers, skate stabbers, after a tale from 1653: a carter lost a skate in Laar, and the people of Weert, who had never seen such a fish, took it for the devil with its mean eyes and pointed tail. The bells rang, the civic guard turned out and a cannon was brought along. Jan, son of the landlord of 't Bruyne Paerd, finally stuck the beast on his pitchfork. Then the carter came back and laughed at them heartily.
Museum voor cultuurhistorie en hedendaag: A museum of cultural history and contemporary art in the former town hall, a national monument. Until 2020 it was the Gemeentemuseum Jacob van Horne, after the count who gave Weert its castle and its monastery. It reopened in May 2022 after a rebuild.

Na de dood van de laatste graaf raakte W: After the death of the last count, Weert fell into decline. The canal from Maastricht to 's-Hertogenbosch brought trade back. At Weert it runs west, through the bed of Napoleon's never finished Grand Canal du Nord. The town bridge, the Statterbrök, is as old as the canal: first a drawbridge, from 1913 a swing bridge, and since 1968 today's lift bridge.
Neoromaanse bakstenen kerk van Alphons B: A Romanesque Revival brick church by Alphons Boosten from 1939, with a tower of 45 metres. It was built for the Keent neighbourhood, where the soldiers of the new Van Horne barracks came to live.
Op 20 juli 1879 ging het station open, a: On 20 July 1879 the station opened, on the railway known as the Iron Rhine. Today's brick building, with its octagonal tower and the town's arms on the spire, is from 1914 and was designed by George van Heukelom. Until the late 1960s Weert was a goods station with a shunting engine of its own, the Sik.
Op 22 september 1944 is Weert bevrijd, d: Weert was liberated on 22 September 1944, by British soldiers of the Suffolk Regiment. Suffolkweg across the canal is named after them, and their memorial has stood by the town bridge since 2002.
Philips de Montmorency, graaf van Horne: Philip de Montmorency, count of Horne and lord of Weert, was an admiral and a knight of the Golden Fleece. When Alva came, William of Orange fled; Egmont and Horne stayed. On 5 June 1568 they were beheaded on the Grand Place in Brussels. His gravestone lies in Saint Martin's church, but whether he was buried there is not certain. Since 2022 he sits on horseback in the forecourt of his castle.
Ronde bakstenen beltmolen uit 1883, geno: A round brick mound mill of 1883, named after Saint Oda. Until 2002 the miller ground rye and buckwheat here for a living. After that the mill fell into disrepair, and in 2026 its cap and sails were taken off. Now it is waiting to be restored.
Ruïne van het kasteel van de graven van: Ruin of the castle of the counts of Horne
Toen zijn nieuwe kasteel klaar was, scho: When his new castle was ready, Jacob I of Horne gave his old manor, the Aldenborgh, to the Friars Minor. After his wife died he joined them himself. The late Gothic Paterskerk was built from 1512 to 1526. The French dissolved the friary in 1797; in 1836 the friars came back. They stayed until 2023: after 561 years too few friars were left.
Van deze koren-, pel- en oliemolen uit 1: Only the tower is left of this corn, hulling and oil mill of 1855. It is named after the Boonen family, its owners from 1863 to 1927. As the area behind the station filled with houses the mill caught less and less wind; in the heavy storm of 9 February 1949 the shaft broke. After that the tower carried a large advertisement for Blue Band. The cap came off in 1968.
Weert is een waard: een hoog en droog st: Weert is a waard: a high and dry piece of land among the Peel marshes, where the roads across heath and bog met. The place is first named in a charter of 1062. People lived here long before: on the Boshoverheide lies a large urnfield from the late Bronze Age.
